values.stages.1: Persistent Data and File Round Trips
values.goal: Verify user flows in a separate Node test environment and design data isolation, asynchronous waiting, and diagnostic evidence.
values.capstone: Build a test suite that verifies Frontory navigation, documents, note backup and restoration, preservation on errors, and visual regression on an independent origin.

values.title: Testing from the User’s Perspective
values.prerequisites: Understand DOM roles, asynchronous behavior, and testing basics, and be able to read the inputs and outputs of the existing starting examples.
values.environment: Write and run all tests in a separate Node project using @playwright/test and a dedicated local test origin. The existing playwright-01·02·03 previews only display test source; they do not run Playwright in the iframe. Write new test files yourself for the assignments and judge whether they pass only from actual runner output. Do not use a user profile or storage used for everyday work; preserve CSP and isolation.
values.concepts.0.title: User contract
values.concepts.0.explanation: role and label follow UI meanings that users understand. They express the purpose of an action more clearly than internal class names.
values.concepts.1.title: Auto-waiting
values.concepts.1.explanation: Locator actions and retrying assertions wait for state. Do not guess when the UI is ready with a fixed sleep.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of User contract. Input cases: table of contents selection and the open-document button.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: assertion results for the selected title and dialog visibility. Explain the rationale for handling Auto-waiting, linking it to the code.
values.steps.0: In tests/day-1.spec.ts in a separate practice project, install @playwright/test in a separate Node project and write tests for Frontory’s table of contents and document opening. Refer to the existing Unit 1·14·28 examples only as starting points.
values.steps.1: Input conditions: table of contents selection and the open-document button. Baseline: 1280×800. Run under the baseline conditions, then record observations and errors in notes/day-1.md.
values.steps.2: Variable: viewport; changed value: 390×844. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: assertion results for the selected title and dialog visibility. Hypothesis to check: Verify the same user flow at both sizes. Compare it with the actual results, and record whether they agree and why they differ.
values.variables.0.name: viewport
values.variables.0.expected: Verify the same user flow at both sizes.
values.criteria.0: Required deliverable: assertion results for the selected title and dialog visibility. Results are available for both the baseline and changed conditions, allowing comparison of 2 conditions; input values and the execution environment are recorded together.
values.criteria.1: The explanation of differences between the two conditions connects both concepts: User contract and Auto-waiting. For unexpected items, at least 1 cause or reason they remain unresolved is recorded.
values.questions.0: Which processing stage does User contract affect in this exercise? Input cases: table of contents selection and the open-document button.
values.questions.1: Variable: viewport. Hypothesis to check: Verify the same user flow at both sizes. Did the actual results agree with the hypothesis? Explain the evidence in terms of Auto-waiting.
